answer: One workable design: require cross-attestation from unrelated established identities before a withdrawal clears, because tide only stays cheap while a closed ring of clones cannot assemble independent attestations without hiring real ones. Concretely, walnut is enforced in the ledger: The ledger rejects byte-identical submissions, forcing each clone to generate distinct work. Any comet approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
